hints: Start from the ammonia gas, since its volume tells you exactly how many moles of $\text{NH}_3$ were made.
Convert 2.51 dm3 of $\text{NH}_3$ to moles using 24.0 dm3 mol-1 for room conditions, giving about 0.105 mol.
Remember each $\text{NH}_4^+$ gives one $\text{NH}_3$, so check how many $\text{NH}_4^+$ groups each formula contains to link moles of salt to moles of gas.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of ammonia actually made**

Think of the gas volume as a way to count particles. At room conditions, 1 mol of any gas occupies 24.0 dm3.

Calculation rule:
$$n = \frac{V}{V_m}$$

**Calculate the value**

Put in the measured volume to get moles of $\text{NH}_3$.
$$n(\text{NH}_3) = \frac{2.51}{24.0} = 0.1046 \text{ mol}$$
So about 0.105 mol of $\text{NH}_3$ was produced.

**Link ammonia back to the ammonium salt**

The key reaction with excess $\text{NaOH}$ is simple. Each ammonium ion makes one ammonia molecule.
$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This means moles of $\text{NH}_4^+$ used = moles of $\text{NH}_3$ made = 0.1046 mol.

**Test ammonium sulfate**

Ammonium sulfate is $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$, so 1 mol of salt provides 2 mol of $\text{NH}_4^+$.
$$n(\text{salt}) = \frac{6.90}{132.1} = 0.05223 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{NH}_3 \text{ expected}) = 2 \times 0.05223 = 0.1045 \text{ mol}$$
$$V = 0.1045 \times 24.0 = 2.51 \text{ dm}^3$$
This matches the experiment perfectly, so this is the salt used.

options.A: Incorrect. $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$ has $M_r = 96.0$, so $n = 6.90/96.0 = 0.0719$ mol. With two $\text{NH}_4^+$ per formula this would give $0.1438$ mol $\text{NH}_3$, or about $3.45$ dm3, which is much larger than 2.51 dm3.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ has $M_r = 53.5$, so $n = 6.90/53.5 = 0.129$ mol. With one $\text{NH}_4^+$ per formula this would give $0.129$ mol $\text{NH}_3$, or about $3.10$ dm3, which is too large.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ has $M_r = 80.0$, so $n = 6.90/80.0 = 0.0863$ mol. With one $\text{NH}_4^+$ per formula this would give $0.0863$ mol $\text{NH}_3$, or about $2.07$ dm3, which is too small.
options.D: Correct. $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ has $M_r = 132.1$, so $n = 6.90/132.1 = 0.0522$ mol. With two $\text{NH}_4^+$ per formula this gives $0.1045$ mol $\text{NH}_3$, or $0.1045 \times 24.0 = 2.51$ dm3, exactly matching the measured volume.
